raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.8-27B (and other dense Qwen3.5-architecture hybrids) use 48 v-heads over 16 k-heads in their GDN layers, a v/k head ratio of 3. #34859 taught `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous` to handle non-power-of-two groups through a per-head walk, and enabled ratio 3 on CUDA. The AITER tuple in `qwen3_5.py` was left at `(1, 2, 4, 8)`. On ROCm, every GDN layer of these models therefore still takes the unfused fallback on every forward pass: `torch.split`, two `.contiguous()` copies, and a `torch.cat`.

The kernel itself has no CUDA-specific code on this path, and the existing ratio-3 unit test is already registered for AMD CI.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`: add `3` to `_GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` when `_use_aiter` is set (`(1, 2, 4, 8)` -> `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`), and update the comment. CUDA, CPU and non-AITER HIP are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel is pure data movement. `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_fused_split_head_ratios.py` checks it bit-exactly against plain slicing for ratios 1, 2, 3 and 4. On MI355X (ROCm 7.x, torch 2.11.0+rocm, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), with this branch's source:

```
test_ratio_1 PASSED
test_ratio_2 PASSED
test_ratio_3 PASSED
test_ratio_4 PASSED
4 passed in 4.12s
```

In the same environment, `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5._GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` resolves to `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This change removes two copies and a concat per GDN layer per forward pass on ROCm for ratio-3 models. That is the same path CUDA already takes for this layout. I have not run an end-to-end benchmark for this one-line routing change.

Related: #31091 generalizes the ratio whitelist for every backend. #43366 (draft) skips the split entirely for batched Triton decode by using strided views. This PR is the minimal fix, so that the ROCm prefill/extend path, and decode outside #43366, matches CUDA.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (existing ratio-3 test, already registered for AMD CI)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -186,14 +186,14 @@
 _is_xpu = is_xpu()
 
 # Head-group ratios (num_v_heads // num_k_heads) served by the fused
-# split/reshape/cat Triton kernel. On AMD/aiter the ratio-8 layout is also
-# covered by the fused kernel, which removes the two `.contiguous()` copies
-# plus the `torch.cat` of the unfused fallback. On CUDA the ratio-3 dense 27B
-# layout is handled by the Triton kernel's per-head walk (the CPU fused op
-# still requires a power-of-two group). Other backends keep the original
-# tuple so their control flow is unchanged.
+# split/reshape/cat Triton kernel, which removes the two `.contiguous()`
+# copies plus the `torch.cat` of the unfused fallback. On CUDA and AMD/aiter
+# the ratio-3 dense 27B layout is handled by the Triton kernel's per-head walk
+# (the CPU fused op still requires a power-of-two group). On AMD/aiter the
+# ratio-8 layout is also covered by the fused kernel. Other backends keep the
+# original tuple so their control flow is unchanged.
 _GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS = (
-    (1, 2, 4, 8) if _use_aiter else (1, 2, 3, 4) if _is_cuda else (1, 2, 4)
+    (1, 2, 3, 4, 8) if _use_aiter else (1, 2, 3, 4) if _is_cuda else (1, 2, 4)
 )
 
 cached_get_processor = lru_cache(get_processor)
